subject: Demo follow-up: model-match & structured-output QA plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightdesk.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightdesk.com>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 13:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Thanks for the demo — follow-ups on model fit and JSON output

Thanks for the walkthrough today — the demo was super helpful. Two quick follow-ups from our side so we can scope the POC: 

1) Model recommendations: we need something that reliably produces strict JSON for customer-facing invoices (fixed schema) and can call our payment validation webhook when it detects a card change. Latency target is ~300ms p95 for single-item invoice generation.

2) Quality regressions: we run a nightly validation job against historical prompts. If we switch models or quantize, what are typical regression risks and how do you recommend we guard against them?

3) Retries/structured output: how should we handle transient failures — do you recommend client-side retries, Redwood retries, or both? Also want confirmation on content-type and schema enforcement options (automated schema validation vs. post-hoc eval).

Can you also send the prompt set / example schema you referenced and any benchmark summary so we can kick off legal and infra discussions?

Thanks,
Samir
Head of Product, BrightDesk
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@brightdesk.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jun 2028 15:12:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — follow-ups on model fit and JSON output

Samir — great to meet you and Elena today. Recap + concrete next steps below. Attaching the prompt set and a starter JSON schema for the invoice payload (see attachments). Also included a short benchmark summary from a similar customer.

Quick answers up front:
- Model recommendations (production-friendly):
  • Redwood-curated: Llama-2-13B-chat (safety-tuned) — good balance of quality + latency at short contexts.
  • For stricter JSON and tool-calling: Falcon-40B-instruct (quantized with Redwood Optimize profiles) — stronger structured output when paired with function calling enforcement.
  • If you need an aggressive cost-latency tradeoff: gptj-30b-quant (fast on our dedicated pools) — expect slightly more redo for edge-case validation.

- Regression risk / guardrails:
  • Nightly evals: run the historical prompt suite (attached) with the candidate model + baseline. Redwood Optimize can produce delta reports per metric (schema pass-rate, token-level edit-distance, hallucination score).
  • Canary rollouts: start with 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with rollback triggers if schema pass-rate drops > 1.5% or customer-impacting errors increase.

- Retries & failure handling:
  • Recommended pattern: server-side (Redwood) retries for transient infra errors (idempotent, limited backoff) + client-side de-dup and a bounded retry window. For function/tool calls, prefer Redwood-managed retries so the runtime can maintain consistent KV cache and avoid double side-effects.
  • We can configure automatic JSON-schema enforcement (reject / fallback / auto-rewrite) at the route level. Fallback policy options: retry with stricter prompt + enforce-toolcall, or route to a safe-lightweight model.

Next steps (proposed):
1) We share: prompt_set_v1.json, schema_example_v2.json, benchmark_summary.pdf (attached).
2) BrightDesk runs baseline job (we can share a small runner script) — target: 1000 historical prompts to get initial pass-rate.
3) Redwood spins up a bench run (we'll run the candidate models on a dedicated job and share the delta report).
4) If pass-rate and latency align, we set up a 2-week POC with canary rollout and function-call integration.

Marissa (SRE solutions) — can you add the runner script and a short checklist for infra (VPC, webhook auth, request id headers)? Camila (CS) — can you lead the onboarding/canary plan with BrightDesk?

Samir — attaching the files now. Also adding a HubSpot deal (link below) and a short RFC we’ll reference.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference

Attachments: prompt_set_v1.json, schema_example_v2.json, benchmark_summary.pdf
From: Elena Ruiz <elena.ruiz@brightdesk.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@brightdesk.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 20 Jun 2028 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — follow-ups on model fit and JSON output

Thanks Dylan — this looks good. A couple of clarifying Qs before we run the baseline: 

- Schema enforcement behavior: if the model returns invalid JSON, can Redwood automatically attempt a single constrained rewrite before falling back? We want to avoid extra client-side complexity.

- Side-effect dedup: for webhook calls (payment validation), is there a recommended idempotency key pattern you prefer? We generally use request_id + timestamp but want to align with Redwood retries.

- Bench scope: for the initial run, we’ll provide 1,200 historical prompts (varied lengths). Can your test job include tokenized latency (p50/p95) and the schema pass-rate per prompt type? Also include failure-mode examples where the model returned valid JSON but incorrect enum values.

Finally, can you add estimated cost for the 2-week POC (baseline run + canary traffic on dedicated pool)? We need to budget before legal signs the SOW.

—Elena
Product Manager, BrightDesk

Subject: Re: Thanks for the demo — follow-ups on model fit and JSON output

Elena / Samir — answers and a short plan below.

- Auto-rewrite on invalid JSON: yes — Redwood can run a single automatic constrained rewrite with the following behavior:
  1) Validate against schema_example_v2.json.
  2) If invalid, run a concise rewrite prompt that instructs the model to return strictly the JSON object without prose.
  3) If rewrite still fails, apply fallback policy: route to a stricter model variant or return a 422 to the client with an explicit error tag.

- Idempotency key: recommend a 3-part key: customer_id|request_id|sequence_hash. Redwood will surface the request_id header for retries; you can use request_id + payment_txn_id as a dedupe across retries. We will add server-side dedupe hooks in the POC.

- Bench scope and metrics: we will include p50/p95 token-latency, end-to-end route latency, schema pass-rate, enum-mismatch rate, and a short list of failure-mode examples. We’ll also tag prompts by length bucket for the report.

- POC cost estimate (initial):
  • Baseline run (1,200 prompts across 3 models): ~$1,200 (on Redwood hosted bench pricing).
  • 2-week canary on a small dedicated pool (SLA-lite): ~$6,500 (includes 5% -> 25% traffic ramp).
  • Exact numbers will be in the SOW; legal typically asks for a capped not-to-exceed.

Action items:
- Dylan: schedule bench run and share runner script + Drive link (today).
- Marissa: add runner script + infra checklist (VPC, webhook auth) and estimate time to enable dedicated pool in our env.
- Camila: draft a 2-week canary runbook with rollback triggers (schema pass-rate threshold + error spike criteria).
- Samir / Elena: confirm you’ll deliver the 1,200 historical prompts (CSV + minimal metadata) by Mon 6/25.

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Account Exec, Redwood Inference
